subject: Database Reliability Engineer, Core Team — requisition c3617664
paragraphs: I am applying for the Database Reliability Engineer role in ClickHouse Core. The description asks for someone who improves reliability and performance of the core, builds the metrics and alerts that catch problems before customers see them, and finds root causes deeply enough to file the bug. That is the loop I already run on a much smaller system, and I would like to run it where the scale is real.

I operate thirteen Linux hosts from one declaration, with PostgreSQL as the system of record for a mail archive and an application pipeline. Health is a recording, not a dashboard: CPU, memory and IO pressure, disk headroom, job status and generation age go into a ledger every fifteen minutes, and any state that is not ok pages me. When something breaks I read journald and unit state, check cgroup counters, and reach for tcpdump when the network is lying; the fix is not done until it is a check that runs in CI and on the host. Releases are one step — build, gate, activate — with rollback as a pointer to the previous generation. The tooling is Go and Python behind a single task interface.

On databases specifically: I have run PostgreSQL in production, written the SQL by hand, and kept the schema in the same repository as the Go services that query it. I have read C++ from instrument software at Fraunhofer ISE and can follow it, though I write Go and Python far more than C++. I have not operated ClickHouse, and I have not worked on a distributed database's storage engine, replication or query planner — those are the parts of this role I would be learning rather than bringing.

The rest of the honest list: no chaos engineering programme, no ownership of blameless postmortems in a 24/7 organisation, and no on-call rotation at company scale; my cloud work is a small AWS Lambda project and Oracle Cloud hosts rather than platform ownership across AWS, GCP or Azure. What transfers is the method — measure saturation, alert on state rather than symptoms, keep the causality in the logs, and treat an incident as unfinished until the fix is enforced by a gate. I am in Germany, so the remote option in this posting works without relocation, and I need no sponsorship for a German contract.

I would bring a bias toward evidence and a willingness to be the person who reads the query profile instead of guessing. A conversation about where the core team's reliability gaps actually are would be enough to tell whether that fits.
